subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Making choices
overview: A choice is a decision you make when more than one way is open. In this sub-strand you will list choices you make each day, talk about their results, and learn to choose what is acceptable to God. You will practise responsibility by making right choices at home and at school.

lessons.title: Choices we make each day
objectives: List choices made in day-to-day life.
Tell the difference between a right choice and a wrong choice.
lessons.intro: Every day you decide small things: whether to tell the truth, whether to finish your work, and whether to be kind. Those decisions are choices. God gave people the ability to choose.
lessons.notes:
A choice is picking one action when you could do something else. Some choices are small, such as which game to play at break. Some choices matter a great deal, such as whether to cheat or to obey.

### Choices at home and at school
In pairs, learners can list choices like these:

- Telling the truth or telling a lie
- Doing homework or leaving it undone
- Sharing a rubber or hiding it
- Speaking politely or insulting someone
- Helping a parent or refusing to help
- Coming to school or staying away without a good reason
- Forgiving a friend or planning revenge

You make some choices when nobody is watching. Those choices show who you are becoming.

### Right and wrong
A right choice agrees with what God wants and with the good of other people. A wrong choice breaks God's word or hurts someone. Wanting something does not make it right. A sweet offered by a stranger may look pleasant and still be a dangerous choice.

### How to pause before you choose
Ask three questions. Is this obedient to God and to my parents? Will it help or harm someone? Would I be glad if my teacher saw me do it? If you are not sure, stop and ask a trusted adult. Singing a song about good choices helps the class remember that choosing well is part of Christian life.

keyWords.meaning: a decision to do one thing rather than another

activity.title: List daily choices in pairs
steps: In pairs, list choices you make in day-to-day life at home and at school.
Mark each choice as one that can be right or one that can be wrong.
Share two choices with the class.
Sing a song about good choices.

practice.question: What is a choice?
practice.answer: A decision to do one thing rather than another.

practice.question: Give three choices a Grade 4 learner makes in daily life.
practice.answer: Any three: telling the truth or lying, doing homework or leaving it, sharing or hiding items, speaking politely or insulting, helping parents or refusing, forgiving or taking revenge.

practice.question: Name one question you can ask before you choose.
practice.answer: Any one: Is this obedient to God and my parents? Will it help or harm someone? Would I be glad if my teacher saw me?

summary: A choice is a decision between two or more actions.
You make choices at home and at school every day.
A right choice agrees with God's word and does not harm others.

lessons.title: Results of the choices we make
objectives: Discuss the results of choices made in daily life.
Give an example of a good result and a harmful result.
lessons.intro: A choice does not stop when you make it. It leads somewhere. Telling the truth may bring trust. Taking what is not yours may bring shame. The result is the effect of the choice.
lessons.notes:
Every choice has a result. The result may come at once or later. A learner who revises may pass a test. A learner who copies may be caught and lose the teacher's trust. Both results grew out of a choice.

### Good results
- Honesty builds trust. People believe you next time.
- Hard work builds skill. You learn to read, write and solve problems.
- Kindness builds friendship. Classmates want to work with you.
- Obedience keeps you safe. You avoid dangers your parents warned you about.
- Forgiveness brings peace in the family.

### Harmful results
- A lie may be found out, and people stop trusting you.
- Fighting can cause injury and punishment.
- Refusing to help at home leaves more work for others and brings conflict.
- Going with a stranger can put you in danger.
- Staying angry can spoil a friendship.

### Talking about effects
When you discuss results, do not only say "it is bad." Say what happens next. "If I hide my friend's pen, she cannot write, and I have stolen." That sentence shows the effect. "If I return the pen, she can work, and I stay honest."

You cannot always undo a result, so think before you act. If you have already chosen wrongly, tell the truth, say sorry and choose differently next time. That new choice also has a result: forgiveness and a fresh start.

keyWords.meaning: what happens because of a choice; the effect
the outcome that follows an action

examples.problem: Kiptoo finds a fifty-shilling coin on the classroom floor. What are two possible choices and their results?
steps: He can keep it secretly. The result is that the owner loses the money and Kiptoo becomes dishonest.
He can give it to the teacher. The result is that the owner may get it back and Kiptoo is trustworthy.
examples.answer: Keeping it harms the owner and trains dishonesty. Handing it in can restore the money and builds trust.

activity.title: Match choices with their results
steps: In groups, write five choices learners make at school.
Beside each choice, write one likely result.
Sort the results into helpful and harmful.
Tell the class one harmful result you want to avoid this week.

practice.question: What is a result of a choice?
practice.answer: What happens because of the choice; its effect.

practice.question: Give one good result of telling the truth.
Give one harmful result of fighting.
practice.answer: Someone may be injured, and you may be punished.

summary: Every choice leads to a result.
Good choices can bring trust, skill, friendship, safety and peace.
Harmful choices can bring shame, injury, conflict or danger.

lessons.title: Right choices that please God
objectives: Make right choices guided by the word of God.
Show responsibility by choosing what is right.
lessons.intro: Christians do not choose only by what feels easy. They ask what God's word says. A responsible learner does the right thing even when friends choose something else.
lessons.notes:
The word of God is the Holy Bible. It guides choices. It tells us to tell the truth, to honour parents, to love our neighbour, to forgive, and to keep away from what is impure. When a choice is hard, open the Bible or remember a verse you have learnt.

### Choices acceptable to God
A choice acceptable to God is one He approves. Examples:

- Returning a lost item instead of keeping it
- Refusing to cheat in a test
- Saying no to a stranger who offers gifts
- Helping a classmate who has no pencil
- Stopping a quarrel instead of spreading it
- Obeying parents and teachers

Friends may laugh. Do the right thing anyway. Responsibility means you accept the duty to choose well, and you accept the result.

### How the Bible guides you
Before you act, recall a lesson you know. Ephesians 4:26 guides you not to sin in anger. Philippians 4:4 guides you to rejoice rather than sulk. Genesis 1:27 guides you to respect every person as God's creation. You do not need to know every chapter. Use the verses you have already learnt, and ask a Sunday school teacher when you are unsure.

### Portraying responsibility
Portray means to show by the way you live. You portray responsibility when you:

- Do your own homework
- Admit a mistake without being forced
- Keep a promise
- Encourage a friend to make a right choice too

Role-play a scene: one learner invites another to copy answers. The second learner says, "No. I will do my own work. That choice is acceptable to God." Then sing a song about good choices so the class remembers the lesson.

keyWords.meaning: doing your duty and accepting the results of your choices
a choice that agrees with God's word

activity.title: Role-play right choices
steps: In groups, role-play making right choices that are acceptable to God, such as refusing to cheat, returning a lost item, or saying no to a stranger.
After each scene, the class says which verse or lesson guided the choice.
Each learner writes one right choice he or she will make this week.
Sing a song about good choices.

practice.question: What guides a Christian when making a choice?
practice.answer: The word of God, the Holy Bible.

practice.question: Give two choices that are acceptable to God.
practice.answer: Any two: telling the truth, returning a lost item, refusing to cheat, saying no to a stranger, helping a classmate, obeying parents, forgiving.

practice.question: How does a learner portray responsibility?
practice.answer: By doing the right thing, doing his or her own work, admitting mistakes and keeping promises.

summary: The Bible guides Christians to make right choices.
A choice acceptable to God agrees with His word.
Responsibility means doing right even when others do not.

quiz.question: A choice is...
options: a decision to do one thing rather than another
quiz.explanation: Choosing means picking one action when another was possible.

quiz.question: Which of these is a day-to-day choice?
options: The name of a Bible book you have not opened
A story from another country you have not read
quiz.explanation: Telling the truth or lying is a choice learners meet every day.

quiz.question: What is a result?
quiz.answer: What happens because of a choice.
quiz.explanation: The effect that follows an action is its result.

quiz.question: What is a likely result of always telling the truth?
What is a harmful result of going with a stranger who offers gifts?
options: You may be put in danger
quiz.explanation: Accepting a stranger's gifts and going with them can lead to harm.

quiz.question: What should guide a Christian's choices?
quiz.explanation: Right choices are guided by the Bible.

quiz.question: Which choice is acceptable to God?
options: Returning a lost coin to the teacher
quiz.explanation: Returning what is lost is honest and pleases God.

quiz.question: A friend says, "Copy my answers." What is the responsible reply?
quiz.answer: No. I will do my own work.
quiz.explanation: Responsibility means choosing what is right even when a friend chooses wrongly.

quiz.question: Portraying responsibility means...
options: showing by your life that you do what is right
letting others decide everything for you
quiz.explanation: To portray responsibility is to live it out in daily choices.

quiz.question: You find a classmate's rubber. Which pair is correct?
quiz.answer: The right choice is to return it. The result is honesty and a classmate who can work.
quiz.explanation: The choice and its result belong together.
